reasoning: The September 2020 meeting formally adopted flexible average inflation targeting (FAIT) as the new reaction function, replacing the prior symmetric 2% target framework. The statement introduced outcome-based forward guidance explicitly linking rate liftoff to labor market and inflation thresholds ('until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time'), a materially different and more dovish commitment than the July language of maintaining rates 'until it is confident that the economy has weathered recent events.' This represents a genuine regime shift in the reaction function — not merely a language polish — as it codifies a new asymmetric inflation strategy and raises the bar for tightening.
key_quote: With inflation running persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent.
